In Brugada Syndrome (BrS) and idiopathic ventricular fibrillation (IVF), isoproterenol remains the therapeutic gold standard for suppressing ES, occasionally supplemented by quinidine.

Conversely, catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT) represents a unique challenge where the adrenergic surge is the primary driver; here, therapy centres on the radical withdrawal of catecholamines, including the avoidance of epinephrine even during resuscitation and the absolute reliance on high-dose beta-blockade.
